name: Juan Ruiz, Arcipreste de Hita
credit: A folio of a medieval manuscript of the Libro de buen amor — a manuscript page, not a portrait, as no likeness of the poet exists · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Juan Ruiz (c. 1283–c. 1350), Archpriest of Hita, a town in the province of Guadalajara, is the author of the Libro de buen amor, the greatest poem of medieval Castile. Almost everything known of his life is drawn from the book itself, which says that he was born in Alcalá de Henares and which a later note claims was finished in prison, by order of the Archbishop of Toledo, in 1343.

The Libro de buen amor is a fictional autobiography in cuaderna vía and in lyric metres, mixing love-stories, beast-fables, parodies of the church year, songs to the Virgin and the mountain-girl songs known as cantigas de serrana. Its title plays on the difference between the good love of God and the mad love of the world.
